questions.title: Sort Parcel Packs by Count Then Price
questions.description:
A warehouse sorts parcel packs: primary key piece COUNT ascending, and for equal counts the MORE EXPENSIVE pack first (price descending) so premium stock ships first. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int[][] sortPacks(int[][] packs)

packs[i] is {count, price}. It must return the ordered array. Sorting helpers are forbidden.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: 2n integers count1 price1 count2 price2 ....

Output Format:
One line with the ordered packs flattened: count1 price1 count2 price2 ....

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, 1 <= count <= 1000, 1 <= price <= 100000

questions.title: Sort Orders by Frequency Then Value
questions.description:
A complaint desk groups repeated order codes: codes that occur LESS often come first, and equal-frequency codes are ordered by ascending value. Values are between 1 and 100. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int[] sortByFrequency(int[] arr)

It must return a new array: increasing frequency, ties by increasing value. Sorting helpers are forbidden.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated order codes.

Output Format:
One line with the reordered array, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 200, 1 <= arr[i] <= 100

questions.title: Stable Even-Odd Rearrangement
questions.description:
A traffic console separates even-recorded vehicles from odd ones while PRESERVING the relative order inside each group (a stable partition): all evens first, then all odds. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int[] evensFirstStable(int[] arr)

It must return a new array holding all even values in their original order followed by all odd values in their original order. Sorting helpers are forbidden.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the rearranged array, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 500, -1000 <= arr[i] <= 1000

questions.title: Bubble Versus Selection Swaps
questions.description:
A lab measures both classics on the same data: report the selection-sort swap count AND the bubble-sort swap count. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static long[] swapComparison(int[] arr)

It must return {selectionSwaps, bubbleSwaps} — selection swaps only when the suffix minimum is not already in place; bubble swaps every inverted adjacent pair. Use working copies. The harness prints both numbers.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the selection swaps, then the bubble swaps, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 200, -1000 <= arr[i] <= 1000

questions.title: Sort by Absolute Value
questions.description:
A signal processor sorts readings by absolute magnitude (ascending); when magnitudes are equal the SMALLER (more negative) value comes first. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int[] sortByAbs(int[] arr)

It must return a new array sorted by |value| ascending, ties by value ascending. Sorting helpers are forbidden.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the sorted array, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 500, -1000 <= arr[i] <= 1000

questions.title: Sort Words by Length Then Name
questions.description:
A dictionary app orders entries by word LENGTH first and alphabetically for equal lengths — with a hand-written comparator (no sort helpers). The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static String[] sortWords(String[] words)

It must return a new array ordered by increasing length, ties broken lexicographically (ascending). Sorting helpers are forbidden.

Input Format:
Line 1: k. Line 2: k space-separated lowercase words.

Output Format:
One line with the ordered words, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= k <= 100, 1 <= word length <= 20, lowercase letters only

kiwi fig date cherry banana apple

questions.title: Bubble Sort the Array
questions.description:
Implement the classic bubble sort: repeatedly swap adjacent out-of-order pairs until the array is ascending. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static void bubbleSort(int[] arr)

Sort arr in place (ascending). The harness prints the array afterwards.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the sorted array, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 500, -1000 <= arr[i] <= 1000

questions.title: Selection Sort the Array
questions.description:
Implement selection sort: find the minimum of the unsorted suffix and swap it into place, growing the sorted prefix. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static void selectionSort(int[] arr)

Sort arr in place (ascending). The harness prints the array afterwards.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the sorted array, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 500, -1000 <= arr[i] <= 1000

questions.title: Insertion Sort the Array
questions.description:
Implement insertion sort: take each element and slide it left into its sorted position. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static void insertionSort(int[] arr)

Sort arr in place (ascending). The harness prints the array afterwards.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the sorted array, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 500, -1000 <= arr[i] <= 1000

questions.title: Count Bubble Swaps
questions.description:
Bubble sort performs exactly one swap per inverted pair, so the swap count equals the number of inversions. Count the swaps a full bubble sort would make on the array. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static long bubbleSwaps(int[] arr)

It must return the number of swaps (use a working copy; do not modify the original). Use long maths.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the swap count.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 500, -1000 <= arr[i] <= 1000

questions.title: Count Selection Swaps
questions.description:
Selection sort swaps the current slot with the minimum of the suffix — but only when the minimum is not already in place. Count those swaps. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int selectionSwaps(int[] arr)

It must return the number of swaps a standard selection sort performs (use a working copy).

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the swap count.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 500, -1000 <= arr[i] <= 1000

questions.title: Count Insertion Shifts
questions.description:
Insertion sort shifts elements right while sliding the key into place. Count the shifts — they equal the number of inversions as well. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static long insertionShifts(int[] arr)

It must return the number of shift operations (use a working copy). Use long maths.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the shift count.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 500, -1000 <= arr[i] <= 1000

questions.title: Rank the Runners
questions.description:
A race marshal sorts finish times (lower is better) — but the display wants the strongest runner first, so scores are sorted DESCENDING with selection logic. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static void sortByScoreDesc(int[] scores)

Sort scores in place in descending order (pick the maximum of the suffix each pass). The harness prints the array afterwards.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated scores.

Output Format:
One line with the scores in descending order, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 500, 0 <= scores[i] <= 1000

questions.title: Queue by Age (Copy Sort)
questions.description:
A clinic must not disturb its original register, so it produces a sorted COPY of the age list with insertion sort. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int[] sortAgesCopy(int[] ages)

It must return a NEW sorted array (ascending) and leave the original untouched. The harness prints the returned array.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated ages.

Output Format:
One line with the sorted copy, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 500, 1 <= ages[i] <= 120

questions.title: Sort Map Points by X Then Y
questions.description:
A map tool orders landmarks: primary key x ascending, secondary key y ascending — hand-rolled selection sort on coordinate pairs. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int[][] sortPoints(int[][] points)

points[i] is a {x, y} pair. It must return the ordered array (pairs may be the same inner arrays, order matters). Sorting helpers are forbidden.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: 2n integers x1 y1 x2 y2 ....

Output Format:
One line with the ordered pairs flattened: x1 y1 x2 y2 ....

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, -1000 <= coordinate <= 1000

questions.title: Does the Shelf Need Sorting?
questions.description:
A warehouse scanner only triggers the sorting robot when some adjacent pair of prices is out of order. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int needsSorting(int[] prices)

It must return 1 when any prices[i] > prices[i + 1] exists, and 0 when the shelf is already non-decreasing.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated prices.

Output Format:
One line with 1 or 0.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 1 <= prices[i] <= 10000

questions.title: Sorter Comparison Budget
questions.description:
A procurement form asks how many comparisons a standard selection sort performs on n items — always n * (n - 1) / 2, regardless of order. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static long selectionComparisons(int n)

It must return n * (n - 1) / 2 as a long.

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with the comparison count.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000

questions.title: Trace K Bubble Passes
questions.description:
A sorting tutor replays bubble sort pass by pass. One standard pass sweeps every adjacent pair left to right, swapping out-of-order neighbours. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int[] bubbleAfterKPasses(int[] arr, int k)

Perform EXACTLY k standard passes on a working copy and return the array. The harness prints the result.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers. Line 3: k.

Output Format:
One line with the array after k bubble passes, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 200, 0 <= k <= n - 1, -1000 <= arr[i] <= 1000

questions.title: Trace K Selection Passes
questions.description:
The tutor now replays selection sort: pass i scans the suffix from i to the end, finds its minimum, and swaps it into slot i. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int[] selectionAfterKPasses(int[] arr, int k)

Perform EXACTLY k selection passes on a working copy and return the array. The harness prints the result.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers. Line 3: k.

Output Format:
One line with the array after k selection passes, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 200, 0 <= k <= n - 1, -1000 <= arr[i] <= 1000

questions.title: Trace K Insertion Steps
questions.description:
The tutor replays insertion sort up to processing the k-th element: elements at indices 1..k-1 have been inserted into the sorted prefix. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int[] insertionAfterK(int[] arr, int k)

On a working copy, run the insertion loop for i = 1 .. k - 1 only, and return the array. The harness prints the result.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers. Line 3: k (1 <= k <= n).

Output Format:
One line with the partially insertion-sorted array, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 200, 1 <= k <= n, -1000 <= arr[i] <= 1000
